# Pandamonium v1.0.73

This hotfix restores normal, data-preserving updates for Pandamonium installations with large file inventories. Backup manifests remain strictly bounded and fully verified. Rollback is signed v1.0.72 or the retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-973 — Verify large backup manifests without rejecting valid snapshots

### Problem

The backup writer could create a valid manifest larger than the verifier's fixed 16 MiB read limit. CT103 therefore rejected its own 23,145,515-byte manifest covering 58,587 files and 2,324,588,965 payload bytes while safely leaving v1.0.71 active.

### Implementation

Backup generation and verification now share one explicit 64 MiB manifest limit. The writer uses compact JSON and rejects output beyond that limit; the reader preserves every archive-member, schema, path, digest, and payload-integrity check while reporting precise regular-file, size-limit, and unreadable-manifest failures.

### Product value and UI visibility

The existing updater can now complete backup verification for large valid installations instead of stopping at the confirm-version stage. No visual or interaction design changed.

### Verification

Focused backup and updater coverage passed 45 checks. The authoritative local suite passed 6,526 tests with 4 skips, and the Chromium suite passed all 190 tests. Protected PR CI passed Python, browser, syntax, dependency, secret, workflow, container, and image gates. The retained CT103 failure archive also passed a complete read-only verification of all 58,587 files, payload bytes, and digests under the corrected bound.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No schema, environment variable, authentication, or backup-format change was introduced. Existing backups remain compatible. Manifests larger than 64 MiB still fail closed. Rollback remains signed v1.0.72 and the updater's retained snapshot.
